h1:
10 Great Stays
in Central Phetchabun
That We've Already Reviewed
heroSub: 10 hand-picked Phetchabun stays we've reviewed in depth — from a warm-design boutique B&B in the town centre and a hotel with a pool to budget guesthouses under ฿1,000 and a whole-house rental near Ban Na Chaliang. Prices start at about ฿400–2,500/night.
introH2: 🏙️ How many kinds of stay does Phetchabun have, and how do you pick the right one?
introHtml: Phetchabun is a province where you can feel cool, easygoing air almost all year round, and it's not too far from Bangkok — close enough to drive up for a Saturday–Sunday trip, which has made it a favourite for people who want to escape the city and breathe. But when it comes to choosing where to stay, a lot of people get confused, because "a stay in Phetchabun" can mean very different things — in town there are warm-design boutique B&Bs, older hotels with a pool, budget guesthouses under ฿1,000, and design hotels where every room has a balcony, while just outside town there's a whole-house rental near Ban Na Chaliang and roadside hotels around Bueng Sam Phan that work as a stopover. This article gathers 10 Phetchabun stays we've reviewed in depth, kept in the same order as the original article — both the in-town group you can walk to the market from and the out-of-town group that leans into privacy. Every one comes from reading real guest reviews, with the upsides and the honest caveats laid out, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links for each. We'll be straight with you: even though the headline says "central" as in the original, a few places on the list sit outside the town centre, so we've spelled out each one's real location clearly.
mrtHtml: Phetchabun has no metro and limited public transport in town, so having your own car or a rental is by far the easiest way to get around. The stays on this list fall into three location groups: in Phetchabun town (Nai Mueang subdistrict) — a few minutes' walk or drive to the market area, the City Pillar Shrine, Wat Mahathat and Phetcha Bura Buddhist Park, ideal as a base before heading up the mountains (A Day In Phetchabun, Kosit Hill, Dusita Residence, The De Hotel, Klang Muang River Home); the Sadiang area, just outside town — a few kilometres out, quieter, with rice-field views (SR Residence, Sabaidee Place); and Nong Phai and Bueng Sam Phan — further south outside town, good as a stopover or for groups (Bestiny, Villa Nachalieng, Kosit One). From the town centre it's about 40–50 min up to Khao Kho, about 1.5 hours to Phu Thap Boek, and about 1 hour to Si Thep Historical Park.

entries.name: A Day In Phetchabun
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Phetphatthana Rd, Nai Mueang · walk to in-town temples and the church
entries.addr: 34 Phetphatthana Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang District, Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: If you want to sleep in central Phetchabun in a place with design and care behind it, not just a plain roadside room, plenty of reviews put A Day In Phetchabun among the first choices. This is a 3-star boutique Bed & Breakfast that many people call one of the first boutique B&Bs in town, set on Phetphatthana Road in Nai Mueang, with 40 rooms across 5 types — from a Standard Double with a King bed for couples or solo travellers up to a Gang Room with two Queen beds for four. Two things come up most consistently in the reviews — first, the breakfast, made fresh in both Thai and American styles, which many say is better than expected for a stay at this price, and second, the staff, who look after you so attentively it feels like staying with relatives; some international reviewers even say the team here is among the best they've met in Thailand, speaking English and recommending places to visit. The rooms are done in a warm, contemporary boutique style — clean, simple and easy on the eye — and many look out over greenery; on Trip.com the location category reaches 9.0 and service 8.9. A highlight still rare in a smaller province is the wide free parking with an EV charging point, handy for people driving up to Khao Kho, plus a garden and a playground so families can bring small children with peace of mind. The central location means that come evening you're only a few minutes' walk or drive from the market and restaurants, and it makes a convenient base before heading up to Khao Kho (about 40–50 min) or Phu Thap Boek (about 1.5 hours). Honest caveats from the reviews: the bathroom fixtures in some rooms are starting to show their age, the shower pressure in some rooms isn't strong, the breakfast portion on some days is fairly small as it's a set rather than a big buffet, and there's no pool or in-house gym here as it's positioned as an in-town B&B. If you want quiet, ask for a garden-view room rather than a street-view one when you book. In short, it's good value among accessible boutique B&Bs, ideal for anyone who wants to sleep in the town centre in a warm, home-like stay with a well-made breakfast.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for a garden-view room away from the road when you book. Get up in time for breakfast, since it's the standout the reviews praise, and if you're driving an EV, let the hotel know about the charging point in advance.
pros: Warm-design boutique B&B, clean quiet rooms that feel like home, highest score on the list
Fresh Thai-American breakfast, many reviews say better than expected
Friendly, attentive staff who communicate well in English
Free parking with EV charger · garden and playground
cons: No pool or in-house gym, as it's an in-town B&B
Bathroom fixtures in some rooms are ageing, shower pressure weak in some rooms
Street-facing rooms get some daytime traffic noise (from reviews)

entries.type: 3-star hotel · town centre · with a pool
entries.name: Kosit Hill Hotel
entries.revCount: Around 7.5 across several sites · 70 reviews · TripAdvisor #3 in Phetchabun
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Samakkhi Chai Rd, Nai Mueang · ~900 m to the market, walkable
entries.addr: 39 Samakkhi Chai Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang District, Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: Kosit Hill Hotel is a large 3-star hotel that Phetchabun locals and road-trippers have known for years. Set on Samakkhi Chai Road in the town centre, it has around 143 rooms split across two buildings — the Phu Thip building and the Phu Thon building — only about 900 metres from the market area and the centre of town, so come evening you can walk out for food without driving. Its selling point over many in-town stays is the outdoor pool — not many places in Phetchabun town have a real pool — so families with small children love it; on top of that there's an in-house restaurant, meeting rooms and a large convention hall that people in the province often use for banquets and weddings, plus sports corners like table tennis, snooker and a basketball court. The thing that earns the most consistent praise is the friendly, smiling, helpful staff, along with the big, comfortable beds; many say the rooms are spacious and good value, and the front desk is open 24 hours so late arrivals and early departures are easy. TripAdvisor ranks it #3 of 13 hotels in Phetchabun. We have to be straight with you: the building and the décor are fairly old, and plenty of reviews use the phrase "old but clean" — if you're after a brand-new, spotless hotel in every corner, this may not match what you pictured. Honest caveats that come up repeatedly: there are few power outlets in the rooms, making it hard to charge several devices at once, some rooms have no kettle or hairdryer, the bathroom cleanliness in some rooms isn't consistent, and the breakfast is fairly ordinary. Our advice is to bring your own power strip, and to ask for a room in a building or on a floor that's recently been renovated when you book. In short, it suits people who weight function — the pool, parking and a spacious room at a budget price — over how new the room is, especially families who drive in and groups coming for meetings.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The hotel has 2 buildings and several room tiers, so try asking for a room in a recently renovated building or floor facing the mountain view. If you need to charge a lot of devices, bring your own power strip, and walk out to eat in town since the breakfast is fairly ordinary.
pros: Has an outdoor pool, which few stays in Phetchabun town have
Large hotel, lots of rooms, fits groups and families, has meeting rooms
Friendly, helpful staff, big comfortable beds, spacious rooms
Free parking, in-town location walkable to the market, good value
cons: Building and rooms are ageing, look old in places (old but clean)
Few power outlets in the rooms, some rooms have no kettle or hairdryer
Breakfast is fairly ordinary · without your own car, calling public transport isn't convenient

entries.name: Dusita Residence
entries.badge: 🪟 Rooms with a city-view balcony · easy to book
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Phloen Phatthana Rd, Nai Mueang · ~760 m from the town centre
entries.addr: 9/6 Phloen Phatthana Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang District, Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: Dusita Residence is a compact residence in Phetchabun town, on Phloen Phatthana Road in Nai Mueang, about 760 metres from the centre of town and the market area, walkable for food. What makes it appealing for anyone after an in-town stay is the rooms with a private balcony looking over the city, letting you sit out and catch the cool breeze in the morning or evening, plus a reception open 24 hours where the staff speak both Thai and English, so late arrivals and international travellers can relax. Rooms range from a Standard Double with one big bed for couples or solo travellers, a Standard Twin with two single beds for friends or anyone who wants separate beds, up to a Superior Room with more space for those who want more room than usual; every room has a city-view balcony. On Booking.com it scores 8.5 and on Agoda 8.4 from around 68 reviews, which is a strong showing among accessible residences. The in-town location makes it a convenient base before heading up to Khao Kho (about 40–50 min) or Phu Thap Boek (about 1.5 hours), close to the City Pillar Shrine, Wat Mahathat and the archaeology hall within a short drive, with free parking for those who drive in. To be straight with you, this is a small residence with only a handful of rooms, not a big hotel with a pool or full resort-style facilities — it leans on simplicity, cleanliness and the in-town location instead. It's best for couples, solo travellers and tourists who want a clean room with a balcony in town at a reasonable price, ready to walk out and explore Phetchabun's food and markets.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room whose balcony faces an open city view when you book, so you get the breezy morning-and-evening atmosphere. It's a residence with few rooms and fills up fast in winter, so book ahead and compare Booking against Agoda.
pros: Rooms with a private city-view balcony, easy breezy atmosphere
24-hour reception, staff communicate in Thai and English
In-town location, walk to the market, works as a base before the mountains
Accessible starting price, free parking
cons: Small residence, only a few rooms, no pool
Simple facilities, not as full as a big hotel
Rooms fill up fast in winter as numbers are limited

entries.name: The De Hotel by 257 Group
entries.badge: 🎨 Design hotel, every room has a balcony
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Soi Phetcha Bura, Nai Mueang · near the Phetcharat junction
tags: 🚿 Deluxe rooms with a clear glass partition
entries.addr: 3/52 Soi Phetcha Bura, Nai Mueang, Mueang District, Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: The De Hotel by 257 Group is a design hotel in Phetchabun town, easy to spot by its bright indigo-painted five-storey building set against the many clear glass windows fitted to every room, located on Soi Phetcha Bura in Nai Mueang, near the Phetcharat junction and the centre of town. What sets it apart from the usual in-town stay is that every room has a balcony to step out, get some air and look over the city, and the Deluxe-tier rooms are done in a modern style with the shower zone partitioned off by clear glass, which looks more stylish than hotel rooms at a similar price; the furniture leans on wood-and-concrete built-in tones that look clean and contemporary. The starting prices are among the lightest on the list — a Standard Double from about ฿620, a Standard Twin for friends from about ฿720, and a Deluxe design room from about ฿850, every room with a balcony. On Agoda it scores 8.1 and on Booking 8.0 from around 96 reviews, a steady showing among budget design hotels. There's free parking on site, and the in-town location means it's a few minutes' drive to the clock tower and Phetchabun market, about 10 minutes to Phetcha Bura Buddhist Park, and it works well as a base before heading up to Khao Kho (about 40–50 min) or Phu Thap Boek (about 1.5 hours). To be straight with you, this is rated a 2-star hotel, leaning on design rooms at a budget price more than full resort-style facilities, with no pool, and rooms facing the soi may get some traffic noise. It's best for couples, groups of friends and working travellers who want a design room with a balcony in town, at a light price and easy to get around.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want the stylish touch, try booking the Deluxe with the shower zone partitioned by clear glass, but if you're travelling with people you're not close to, pick a Standard room instead. Ask for a higher-floor room whose balcony faces an open view to avoid soi traffic noise and get a better city view.
pros: Among the lightest starting prices on the list, from about ฿620
Every room has a balcony, Deluxe rooms in a modern design with a clear glass partition
In-town location, near the Phetcharat junction and the market, free parking
Steady scores, Agoda 8.1 · Booking 8.0
cons: Rated 2-star, leans on budget design rooms, no pool
Design rooms partition the shower zone with glass, not ideal for groups who aren't close
Rooms facing the soi may get some traffic noise

entries.name: SR Residence Hotel
entries.badge: 🏊 New clean rooms, a pool, rice-field views
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sadiang, Mueang District · ~2 km from town (~7 min drive)
entries.storyHtml: SR Residence Hotel is a 3-star hotel with new, clean rooms in the Sadiang area, about 2 kilometres or roughly a 7-minute drive from Phetchabun town, so you get both the convenience of being close to town and an atmosphere quieter than the centre. It's a multi-storey building, and on arrival you drive up a rise to drop passengers first before parking in the lot, which becomes part of the charm, since the hotel sits on ground that looks out over rice fields and the mountains around town. The thing reviews talk about most is the large pool up top with a pool bar — go up in the evening or at night and you get lovely views and an easy atmosphere, which is hard to find among stays around Phetchabun. Rooms range from a Standard Twin with twin beds, a roomier Large Standard, up to a Deluxe King, the widest, for couples or a small family; every room has a private balcony to sit out and take in the view, and the rooms are fairly new and clean compared with older hotels in town. On Agoda it scores 8.6 and on Booking 8.5 from over 900 reviews combined — the highest review count on the list — reflecting how steadily people stay here and review it. There's wide free parking, and the Sadiang location works as a base before heading up to Khao Kho (about 40 min) or out to Si Thep Historical Park (about 1 hour). The thing to keep in mind is that it isn't right in the town centre — to reach the market or restaurants in town you'll need a short drive, you can't walk there as you would from a central stay. It's best for those who want a new, clean room with a pool and rice-field views at a mid-range price and who drive in themselves.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room whose balcony faces the rice-field and mountain view, and head up to the pool and pool bar in the evening for the best atmosphere. Since it's a bit outside town, plan dinner in town ahead, as you'll need to drive out.
pros: Rooms are fairly new and cleaner than older hotels in town
Has a pool and pool bar, lovely rice-field and mountain views
Every room has a private balcony · wide free parking
Highest review count on the list, Agoda 8.6 · Booking 8.5
cons: In the Sadiang area, ~2 km from town, you need to drive into town
Starting price higher than the in-town guesthouse and boutique group
Can't walk to the market or restaurants in town, you need a car

entries.name: Klang Muang River Home
entries.badge: 🏡 Home-like feel, air-con rooms with a balcony
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Klang Muang Phatthana Rd, Nai Mueang · walk to in-town temples and the church
entries.addr: 53/31 Klang Muang Phatthana Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang District, Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: Klang Muang River Home is a homestay-style guesthouse in Phetchabun town, on Klang Muang Phatthana Road in Nai Mueang, positioned as a home-like stay more than a hotel. It's a 3-storey building, with the reception and common areas designed to feel open and airy, like staying in the home of someone you know — quiet and relaxed even though it's in town. What makes it appealing for budget travellers is the starting price in the ฿600s for an air-con room with a balcony, fridge and work desk; the choices range from a Basic Room for solo travellers or short stays, a Basic Room with a Queen bed for couples, up to a Deluxe Room with a Queen bed that's roomier and better appointed for longer stays, and there's a shared kitchen you can cook in, handy for long stays or saving on food. The location is genuinely walkable — only about 0.3 kilometres from Wat Phetchawararam and the Phetchabun Christian church, an easy walk, and a few minutes' drive to the market area and the centre of town. On Booking.com and Agoda it scores around 7.9, a good score for a guesthouse at this price, but to be straight with you there are only around 6 online reviews, because it's a small stay in a smaller province that not many people know about — not because of the quality. There's free parking for those who drive in, and it works as a base before heading up to Khao Kho (about 40–50 min). The thing to keep in mind is that this is a small home-style guesthouse, with no pool or big-hotel facilities, and a small number of rooms. It's best for budget travellers, couples and anyone who wants a quiet, warm, home-like stay in town with a kitchen to cook in.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're staying several nights or want to save on food, use the shared kitchen to cook for yourself. There are few rooms and it's a small home-style stay, so book ahead and message the host about check-in time, as it isn't a hotel with a 24-hour counter.

Starting price in the ฿600s, air-con room with a balcony, fridge and work desk
Has a shared kitchen to cook in, good for long stays or saving money
Walk to in-town temples and the church · free parking

entries.name: Sabaidee Place
entries.badge: 💰 Clean rooms under ฿1,000, best value on the list
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sadiang, Mueang District · ~3 km from the centre (6–8 min drive)
entries.addr: 9/3 Burakam Kowit Road, Sadiang, Mueang District, Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: Sabaidee Place is a small guesthouse in the Sadiang area of Mueang Phetchabun district, about 3 kilometres or a 6–8 minute drive from the centre of town, which wins people over on value — the best on this list — with a starting price under ฿1,000. The place is neither small nor large, taking a reasonable number of guests, and the rooms are clean with cold air-con, a fridge, TV and a private bathroom in every room; the décor is simple but well looked after. Rooms range from a Double Room with one big bed from about ฿400 for couples or solo travellers, a Twin Room with twin beds from about ฿430 for friends or colleagues, up to a Triple Room for three from about ฿550 for a small family or group of friends, which works out very cheap split per head. What earns it a high score is cleanliness and service that's better than the price — on Booking.com and Agoda it scores as high as 8.7 on both, even though there are only around 6 online reviews, as it's a small stay not many people know. There's a little garden to sit in and wide free parking for those who drive in; the Sadiang location is about 6 minutes from Phetcha Bura Buddhist Park and works as a base before heading up to Khao Kho (about 40–50 min). The thing to keep in mind is that this is a budget guesthouse — no pool, no breakfast, and not right in the town centre, so to reach the market or restaurants in town you'll need a short drive. It's best for budget travellers who drive in themselves, couples and groups of friends who want a clean, cold-air-con room at the lightest price, with easy parking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If three of you are travelling, pick the Triple Room and split it per head to keep it very cheap. It's a guesthouse with no breakfast, so grab food from the market or a convenience store, and since it's a bit outside town, driving in yourself is the easiest way.
pros: Starting price under ฿1,000, the best value on the list
Clean rooms, cold air-con, looked after better than the price, 8.7 on both sites
Has a little garden and wide free parking
Near Phetcha Bura Buddhist Park, works as a base before the mountains
cons: Budget guesthouse, no pool and no breakfast
In the Sadiang area, ~3 km from the centre, you need to drive into town
Few online reviews so far (around 6), as it's a small stay

entries.type: Roadside 3-star hotel · Ban Na Chaliang, Nong Phai
entries.name: Bestiny Hotel & Restaurant Phetchabun
entries.badge: 🍽️ In-house restaurant · stopover before the mountains
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ban Na Chaliang, Nong Phai District · on Highway 21 (outside town)
entries.addr: 828 Na Chaliang, Nong Phai District, Phetchabun (on Highway 21)
entries.storyHtml: Bestiny Hotel & Restaurant Phetchabun is a roadside 3-star hotel in the Ban Na Chaliang area of Nong Phai district, set on Highway 21, about 35–40 kilometres south of Phetchabun town. We'll be straight with you: it isn't in the town centre as the headline says, but it's on the original list and scores well, so we've kept it while spelling out its real location clearly. Its strength is its position as a very good roadside stopover — for people driving up from Bangkok or the south to visit Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek, you can break the trip for a night here before heading up the mountains the next day, and there's an in-house restaurant that's handy for a late dinner on arrival. The building is open and airy with good airflow, the rooms are clean and spacious, around 76 of them, ranging from a Standard Double with a big bed from a promo price of about ฿800 with air-con, a fridge, a flat-screen TV and a coffee maker, a Standard Twin with twin beds, up to a roomier Superior with a balcony in some rooms, plus two-bedroom suites for families or groups. On Agoda and Booking it scores 8.5 on both from around 36 reviews, a good showing for a roadside hotel. There's wide free parking, it's near a convenience store and a local mall in Ban Na Chaliang, Si Thep Historical Park is within driving distance, and it's about 45–60 min up to Khao Kho. The thing to keep in mind is that, being outside town on a highway, you may hear some traffic from the main road at night, and there's no in-town strolling atmosphere like a central stay. It's best for those driving up for a trip who need a stopover before the mountains, plus families and groups who want a spacious, clean room with an in-house restaurant.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Use this as an overnight stopover before heading up Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek the next day, then have dinner at the in-house restaurant if you arrive late. If you're sensitive to noise, ask for a room that doesn't face Highway 21 directly to avoid traffic noise at night.
pros: Clean, spacious rooms, an open and airy building, around 76 rooms
Has an in-house restaurant, handy for a late dinner on arrival
A good stopover before heading up Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek · wide free parking
Good scores, Agoda 8.5 · Booking 8.5
cons: Outside town (Ban Na Chaliang, Nong Phai, ~35–40 km from town)
On Highway 21, you may hear some traffic from the main road at night
No in-town strolling atmosphere like a central stay

entries.type: Whole-house rental · Ban Na Chaliang, Nong Phai
entries.name: Villa Nachalieng
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ban Na Chaliang, Nong Phai District · ~40–50 min drive from town
entries.addr: 182/98 Moo 5, Yang Ngam, Nong Phai District, Phetchabun (Ban Na Chaliang area)
entries.storyHtml: Villa Nachalieng is a standalone house for rent as a whole house in the Ban Na Chaliang area of Nong Phai district, about a 40–50 minute drive from Phetchabun town. Let's be clear that it's outside town, not a central stay as the headline says, but it's on the original list and suits a group stay, so we've kept it while telling you the real location. What sets it apart from the hotels on the list is its private-house nature, rented as a whole — 2 bedrooms with a living area, sleeping several, ideal for a family or group of friends who want their own space without sharing with other guests. It comes fully equipped for a get-together — a full kitchen to cook in, a barbecue grill in the garden for an evening cook-out, a balcony looking out over the mountains, and karaoke to sing along to as a group; on top of that there are free bicycles to use, and this area is popular for cycling trips. On Agoda and Booking it scores 8.6 on both from around 42 reviews, reflecting how much groups who stay love the home atmosphere and the privacy. The whole-house rate starts at about ฿2,500 a night, which looks high next to a single room, but split per person in a group it's very cheap for this kind of stay. There's Wi-Fi and free parking. The thing to keep in mind is that, being a house in a rural area outside town, going out for food or into town means driving, and there's no hotel-style service such as room service or a 24-hour counter. It's best for large families and groups of friends who want a private house to cook, barbecue, sing karaoke and relax privately amid the mountain setting.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Since it's a whole-house rental, coming as a group and splitting the house cost per person works out best value. Bring ingredients for the kitchen and barbecue from town first, as it's a rural area with few shops, and message the host to confirm check-in ahead, as there's no 24-hour counter.
pros: Whole house with 2 bedrooms, private, ideal for groups and families
Full kitchen, barbecue grill and karaoke, everything for a get-together
Mountain-view balcony, free bicycles, quiet rural atmosphere
Cheap split per person in a group · Agoda 8.6 · Booking 8.6
cons: Outside town (Ban Na Chaliang, Nong Phai, ~40–50 min drive)
Whole-house rate from ฿2,500, not ideal for solo travellers or couples
No hotel-style service, you need to drive into town for food

entries.type: 2-star hotel · Bueng Sam Phan District · stopover
entries.name: Kosit One Hotel
entries.badge: 🏔️ Mountain and rice-field views · stopover near Si Thep
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sap Samo Thot, Bueng Sam Phan District · ~40–50 min drive from town

rooms.type: Superior twin beds with a balcony

entries.addr: 379 Moo 9, Sap Samo Thot, Bueng Sam Phan District, Phetchabun
entries.storyHtml: Kosit One Hotel is a 2-star hotel in Bueng Sam Phan district, Sap Samo Thot subdistrict, right on the main road, about a 40–50 minute drive south of Phetchabun town. We'll be straight with you: it isn't in the town centre as the headline says, but it's on the original list and scores well with a good review count, so we've kept it while spelling out its real location. Its strength is being a good stopover for people driving through Bueng Sam Phan, especially those heading to Si Thep Historical Park, a World Heritage site only about a 30–40 minute drive away. The building is 3 storeys done up to feel home-like, the surroundings are natural, looking out over mountains and rice fields, and there are around 41 rooms, clean and simple, many with a balcony to step out and take in the rice-field view. Choices range from a Standard Room of about 24 square metres from about ฿575, a Superior with a balcony from about ฿690, up to a Superior with twin beds and a balcony from about ฿720 — accessible prices that suit a one-night stay on the way. On Agoda it scores 8.5 and on Booking 8.3 from around 396 reviews combined, a high count that reflects steady stopovers and consistent quality. There's free private parking on site. The thing to keep in mind is that, being in an outlying district far from town and the main sights like Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek — which are another roughly 1.5–2 hour drive on — it suits a stopover more than a destination. It's best for people driving through Bueng Sam Phan, those visiting the ancient town of Si Thep, and anyone who wants a clean room with a rice-field-view balcony at a budget price for a stop along the way.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're set on Si Thep Historical Park, use this as an overnight base first, as it's only 30–40 minutes away. Ask for a Superior with a balcony to get the rice-field and mountain view, and plan to drive on another 1.5–2 hours up to Khao Kho if you're continuing.
pros: A good stopover, near the ancient town of Si Thep ~30–40 min
Clean, simple rooms, many with a rice-field- and mountain-view balcony

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting prices from the standard-room range and may change by date and season; we recommend checking the real price and comparing 3 sites before every booking. The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms, not from staying ourselves. The order follows the original article; even though the headline says "central", a few places on the list sit outside the town centre (Bestiny and Villa Nachalieng are in Ban Na Chaliang, Nong Phai district · Kosit One is in Bueng Sam Phan district · SR Residence and Sabaidee Place are in the Sadiang area just outside town) — we've spelled out each one's real location clearly. Phetchabun's high season is winter (November–January), when crowds head up to Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek and stays fill up fast, so book ahead. Phetchabun has no metro and limited public transport in town, so having your own car is by far the easiest way to get around. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about Phetchabun stays

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best stay in Phetchabun town?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. If you measure by score and central atmosphere, A Day In Phetchabun at 8.8 is the highest on the list, a warm-design boutique B&B with a good breakfast. If you want a pool in town, Kosit Hill Hotel is a large hotel with one. If you're after newer rooms and a pool, SR Residence in the Sadiang area. And on a tight budget for a clean room at a light price, Sabaidee Place starts under ฿1,000 and scores 8.7.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Phetchabun stays cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at about ฿400–2,500 per night. The cheapest end is Sabaidee Place from ฿400 and The De Hotel from ฿620. The mid group is Dusita Residence ฿650, Klang Muang River Home ฿652, Kosit One ฿650, A Day In Phetchabun ฿744, Bestiny ฿800 and Kosit Hill ฿850. The higher tier is SR Residence ฿1,100 and Villa Nachalieng ฿2,500 (a whole-house rate, cheap split per person). All prices are approximate starting prices from standard rooms, and may run higher than usual in winter.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay to use as a base before heading up Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek?
faq.a: Stays in Phetchabun town are best as a base before the mountains, since you can fill up on fuel, shop and have breakfast all in one place. From town it's about 40–50 min up to Khao Kho and about 1.5 hours to Phu Thap Boek. In-town options include A Day In Phetchabun, Kosit Hill, Dusita Residence, The De Hotel and Klang Muang River Home. If you're driving up from the south and want to break the trip before reaching town, Bestiny Hotel in Ban Na Chaliang or Kosit One in Bueng Sam Phan make good stopovers.

faq.q: ❓ Which Phetchabun stays have a pool?
faq.a: Not many stays in Phetchabun have a real pool. On this list, the ones with a pool are Kosit Hill Hotel, a large in-town hotel with an outdoor pool good for the kids, and SR Residence Hotel in the Sadiang area with a pool and pool bar up top over rice fields. The other stays on the list lean boutique, guesthouse or rental house, so they have no pool.

faq.q: ❓ Where should a large group or family stay in Phetchabun?
faq.a: If you're a large group that wants private space to cook and get together, Villa Nachalieng is a whole-house rental with 2 bedrooms, a kitchen, a barbecue grill and karaoke, cheap split per person (in the Ban Na Chaliang area, outside town). If you'd rather be in town with a pool for the kids, Kosit Hill Hotel is a large hotel with lots of rooms that fits groups. And A Day In Phetchabun has a Gang Room sleeping 4 plus a playground for families.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get around Phetchabun, and do you need a car?
faq.a: Phetchabun has no metro and limited public transport in town, and hailing a taxi isn't as easy as in a big city, so having your own car or a rental is the easiest way, especially if you plan to head up Khao Kho and Phu Thap Boek or out to Si Thep Historical Park outside town. Most stays on this list have free parking. If you're not driving in, we'd suggest a stay in town you can walk to the market and restaurants from, and planning your travel or asking the hotel about a shuttle in advance.
